what: 3. Fit model and check for convergence
title: Ex 1: The basics
text: default, fit_wham() uses 3 extra Newton steps reduce absolute value gradient (n.newton = 3) estimates standard errors derived parameters (.sdrep = TRUE). fit_wham() also retrospective analysis 7 peels default (.retro = TRUE, n.peels = 7). details, see fit_wham(). need check m1 converged (m1$opt$convergence 0, maximum absolute value gradient vector < 1e-06). title: Ex 2: Recruitment linked to an environmental covariate (Cold Pool Index)
text: Now specify 7 models treat recruitment, CPI process, CPI affects recruitment: Look model table. Ecov_how recent character string approach defining environmental effects recruitment. specify options modeling recruitment environmental covariate(s) using prepare_wham_input() function. WHAM provides 4 options recruitment (recruit_model): random walk, random mean, Beverton-Holt, Ricker. environmental covariate options fed prepare_wham_input() list, ecov: currently 2 options ecov process model (ecov$process_model): 1) random walk ('rw'), 2) autoregressive ('ar1'). Recent versions WHAM now specify effects covariates recruitment, natural mortality, catchability, movement using character strings. recruitment specify recruitment_how mechanistic affect recruitment, time lag covariate recruitment, order orthogonal polynomial effect. options mechanistic effect follow Iles Beverton (1998) Xu et al. (2018): “controlling” (density-independent mortality), “limiting” (carrying capacity, e.g. ecov determines amount suitable habitat), “lethal” (threshold, .e. R –> 0 ecov value), “masking” (metabolic/growth, ecov decreases dR/dS), “directive” (e.g., behavioral). Ecov_how specify lag 1 CPI CPI year t affects recruitment year t + 1. also specify first order polynomial (“linear” “poly-1”). effect covariate, still keeping state-space model estimation covariate, Ecov_how= “none”. can set ecov = NULL process_model= NA fit model without environmental covariate data, note fit ecov data even models without ecov effect recruitment (m1 m3) can compare via AIC (need data likelihood). Options described set_ecov help page. mechanistic effects options implemented every recruitment model.
code: Ecov_how <- paste0(   c("none", "controlling-", "none", "limiting-", "limiting-", "controlling-", "controlling-"),    c("", "lag-1-", "", rep("lag-1-",4)),   c("", "linear", "", rep("linear", 4)))  df.mods <- data.frame(Recruitment = c(2,2,3,3,3,3,4),                       Ecov_process = c(rep("rw",4),rep("ar1",3)),                       Ecov_how = Ecov_how, stringsAsFactors=FALSE) n.mods <- dim(df.mods)[1] df.mods$Model <- paste0("m",1:n.mods) df.mods <- df.mods |> dplyr::relocate(Model) df.mods #>   Model Recruitment Ecov_process                 Ecov_how #> 1    m1           2           rw                     none #> 2    m2           2           rw controlling-lag-1-linear #> 3    m3           3           rw                     none #> 4    m4           3           rw    limiting-lag-1-linear #> 5    m5           3          ar1    limiting-lag-1-linear #> 6    m6           3          ar1 controlling-lag-1-linear #> 7    m7           4          ar1 controlling-lag-1-linear m=1 # example for first model   ecov <- list(     label = "CPI",     mean = as.matrix(env.dat$CPI),     logsigma = as.matrix(log(env.dat$CPI_sigma)),     year = env.dat$Year,     use_obs = matrix(1, ncol=1, nrow=dim(env.dat)[1]), # use all obs (=1)     process_model = df.mods$Ecov_process[m], # "rw" or "ar1"     recruitment_how = matrix(df.mods$Ecov_how[m],1,1)) #matrix for number of stocks (1) and number of Ecovs (1) ?set_ecov

title: Ex 2: Recruitment linked to an environmental covariate (Cold Pool Index)
code: for(m in 1:n.mods){   # set up environmental covariate data and model options   ecov <- list(     label = "CPI",     mean = as.matrix(env.dat$CPI),     logsigma = as.matrix(log(env.dat$CPI_sigma)),     year = env.dat$Year,     use_obs = matrix(1, ncol=1, nrow=dim(env.dat)[1]), # use all obs (=1)     process_model = df.mods$Ecov_process[m], # "rw" or "ar1"     recruitment_how = matrix(df.mods$Ecov_how[m],1,1)) #matrix for number of stocks (1) and number of Ecovs (1)    # (not used in this vignette) can set ecov = NULL to fit model without ecov data   if(is.na(df.mods$ecov_process[m])) ecov = NULL     # generate wham input from ASAP3 and ecov data   input <- prepare_wham_input(asap3, recruit_model = df.mods$Recruitment[m],                               model_name = "Ex 2: SNEMA Yellowtail Flounder with CPI effects on R",                               ecov = ecov,                               NAA_re = list(sigma="rec+1", cor="iid"),                               age_comp = "logistic-normal-pool0") # logistic normal pool 0 obs      # Selectivity = logistic, not age-specific as in ex1   #   2 pars per block instead of n.ages   #   sel pars of indices 4/5 fixed at 1.5, 0.1 (specified via neg phase in ex2_SNEMAYT.dat)   input$par$logit_selpars[1:4,7:8] <- 0 # last 2 rows will not be estimated (mapped to NA)    # Fit model   mod <- fit_wham(input, do.retro=TRUE, do.osa=TRUE)    # Save model   saveRDS(mod, file=paste0(df.mods$Model[m],".rds"))    # Plot output in new subfolder   plot_wham_output(mod=mod, dir.main=file.path(getwd(),df.mods$Model[m]), out.type='html') }

title: Ex 2: Recruitment linked to an environmental covariate (Cold Pool Index)
text: Let’s first make results table prettier. Now get convergence information. calculate AIC Mohn’s rho converged models. Print save results table. m6 lowest AIC (Bev-Holt recruitment, CPI modeled AR1, controlling effect CPI recruitment), m5 m7 similar AIC values.
code: df.mods$Recruitment <- dplyr::recode(df.mods$Recruitment, `2`='Random', `3`='Bev-Holt', `4`='Ricker') df.mods$Ecov_how <- c("---", "Controlling", "---", "Limiting", "Limiting", "Controlling", "Controlling") opt_conv = 1-sapply(mods, function(x) x$opt$convergence) ok_sdrep = sapply(mods, function(x) if(x$na_sdrep==FALSE & !is.na(x$na_sdrep)) 1 else 0) df.mods$conv <- as.logical(opt_conv) df.mods$pdHess <- as.logical(ok_sdrep) df.mods$NLL <- sapply(mods, function(x) round(x$opt$objective,3)) not_conv <- !df.mods$conv | !df.mods$pdHess mods2 <- mods mods2[not_conv] <- NULL df.aic.tmp <- as.data.frame(compare_wham_models(mods2, table.opts=list(sort=FALSE, calc.rho=T))$tab) df.aic <- df.aic.tmp[FALSE,] ct = 1 for(i in 1:n.mods){   if(not_conv[i]){     df.aic[i,] <- rep(NA,5)   } else {     df.aic[i,] <- df.aic.tmp[ct,]     ct <- ct + 1   } } df.mods <- cbind(df.mods, df.aic) df.mods <- df.mods[order(df.mods$dAIC, na.last=TRUE),] df.mods[is.na(df.mods$AIC), c('dAIC','AIC','rho_R','rho_SSB','rho_Fbar')] <- "---" rownames(df.mods) <- NULL df.mods save(df.mods, file="vign2_res.RData") #>   Model Recruitment Ecov_process                 Ecov_how #> 1    m1           2           rw                     none #> 2    m2           2           rw controlling-lag-1-linear #> 3    m3           3           rw                     none #> 4    m4           3           rw    limiting-lag-1-linear #> 5    m5           3          ar1    limiting-lag-1-linear #> 6    m6           3          ar1 controlling-lag-1-linear #> 7    m7           4          ar1 controlling-lag-1-linear

title: Ex 3: Projecting / forecasting random effects
text: Projection options specifed using proj.opts input project_wham(). default settings project 3 years (n.yrs = 3), use average maturity-, weight-, natural mortality--age last 5 model years calculate reference points (avg.yrs), use fishing mortality last model year (use.last.F = TRUE), continue ecov process model (cont.ecov = TRUE). options also described project_wham() help page. WHAM implements four options handling environmental covariate(s) projections. Exactly one must specified proj.opts ecov model: (Default) Continue ecov process model (e.g. random walk, AR1). Set cont.ecov = TRUE. WHAM estimate ecov process projection years (.e. continue random walk / AR1 process). Use last year ecov. Set use.last.ecov = TRUE. WHAM use ecov value terminal year population model projections. Use average ecov. Provide avg.yrs.ecov, vector specifying years average environmental covariate(s) projections. Specify ecov. Provide proj.ecov, matrix user-specified environmental covariate(s) use projections. Dimensions must number projection years (proj.opts$n.yrs) x number ecovs (ncols(ecov$mean)). Note options, original model fit ecov years beyond population model, WHAM use already-fit ecov values projections. ecov model extended least proj.opts$n.yrs years beyond population model, none need specified. WHAM implements six options handling fishing mortality projections. Exactly one must specified proj.opts: (Default) Use last year F. Set use.last.F = TRUE. WHAM use F terminal model year projections. Use average F. Set use.avg.F = TRUE. WHAM use F averaged proj.opts$avg.yrs projections (done M-, maturity-, weight--age). Use F X% SPR. Set use.FXSPR = TRUE. WHAM calculate apply F X% SPR, X set input$data$percentSPR (default = 40%). also percentFXSPR Specify F. Provide proj.F, F vector length = proj.opts$n.yrs. Specify catch. Provide proj.catch, vector aggregate catch length = proj.opts$n.yrs. WHAM calculate F across fleets apply specified catch. Use FMSY. Set use.FMSY = TRUE. WHAM calculate apply F MSY. check make sure stock-recruit model assumed , , F X% SPR used instead. WHAM can also use average “apparent survival” deviations /recruitment deviations apparent survival recruitment deviations projections allows user specify years average different inputs. proj.opts$proj_NAA_opt can specified tell treat apparent survival deviations. proj.opts$proj_R_opt can specify treat recruitment deviations. avg.yrs.R avg.yrs.NAA specify years average deviations using option. Save projected models

text: ASAP data file specifies selectivity options (model, initial parameter values, parameters fix/estimate). WHAM uses default order facilitate running ASAP models. see currently specified selectivity options asap3: specify WHAM model prepare_wham_input(), can overwrite selectivity options ASAP data file optional list argument selectivity. selectivity model chosen via selectivity$model: Regardless selectivity model used, incorporate time-varying selectivity estimating mean selectivity parameter, μas\mu^{s}_a, (random effect) deviations mean, δa,y\delta_{,y}. estimate selectivity parameters, sa,ys_{,y}, logit-scale (possibly) lower upper limits: sa,y=lower+upper−lower1+e−(μas+δa,y)s_{,y} = \mathrm{lower} + \frac{\mathrm{upper} - \mathrm{lower}}{1 + e^{-(\mu^{s}_a + \delta_{,y})}} deviations, 𝛅\boldsymbol{\delta}, follow 2-dimensional AR(1) process defined parameters σs2\sigma^2_s, ρa\rho_a, ρy\rho_y: 𝛅∼MVN(0,Σ)\boldsymbol{\delta} \sim \mathrm{MVN}(0,\Sigma)Σ=σs2(Ra⊗Ry)\Sigma = \sigma^2_s(\mathrm{R}_a \otimes \mathrm{R}_y)Ra,*=ρa|−*|R_{,^*} = \rho_a^{\vert - ^* \vert}Ry,y*=ρy|y−y*|R_{y,y^*} = \rho_y^{\vert y - y^* \vert} Mean selectivity parameters can initialized different values ASAP file selectivity$initial_pars. Parameters can fixed initial values specifying selectivity$fix_pars. Finally, specify time-varying (random effects) selectivity parameters (selectivity$re): loop fit models, first lets define initial parameter values fixed. needed specifically age-specific selectivity models. Now can run models loop:
code: asap3$dat$sel_block_assign # 1 fleet, all years assigned to block 1 #> NULL # by default each index gets its own selectivity block (here, blocks 2 and 3)  asap3$dat$sel_block_option # fleet selectivity (1 block), 2 = logistic #> NULL asap3$dat$index_sel_option # index selectivity (2 blocks), 2 = logistic #> NULL  asap3$dat$sel_ini # fleet sel initial values (col1), estimation phase (-1 = fix) #> NULL asap3$dat$index_sel_ini # index sel initial values (col1), estimation phase (-1 = fix) #> NULL #initial pars for logistic or age-specfic selectivity initial_pars <- c(rep(list(list(c(2,0.3),c(2,0.3),c(2,0.3))),3), rep(list(list(c(0.1,0.5,0.5,1,1,1),c(0.5,0.5,0.5,1,1,0.5),c(0.5,0.5,1,1,1,1))),5)) #which pars to fix for age-specific selectivity fix_pars <- c(list(NULL,NULL,NULL), rep(list(list(4:6,4:5,3:6)),5)) #make a list of fits to fill in mods <- list()  for(m in 1:n.mods){     # overwrite initial parameter values in ASAP data file (ex1_SNEMAYT.dat)     input <- prepare_wham_input(asap3, model_name=paste(paste0("Model ",m), sel_model[m], paste(sel_re[[m]], collapse="-"), sep=": "), recruit_model=2,                 selectivity=list(model=rep(sel_model[m],3), re=sel_re[[m]], initial_pars=initial_pars[[m]], fix_pars = fix_pars[[m]]),                 NAA_re = list(sigma='rec+1',cor='iid'),                 age_comp = "logistic-normal-miss0") # logistic normal, treat 0 obs as missing      # fit model     mods[[m]] <- fit_wham(input, do.check=T, do.osa=F, do.retro=F)  }  #save the model fits for(m in 1:length(mods)) saveRDS(mod[[m]], file=paste0("m",m,".rds"))

code: mods <- list() for(m in 1:n.mods){   ecov <- list(     label = "GSI",     mean = as.matrix(env.dat$GSI),     logsigma = 'est_1', # estimate obs sigma, 1 value shared across years     year = env.dat$year,     use_obs = matrix(1, ncol=1, nrow=dim(env.dat)[1]), # use all obs (=1)     process_model = df.mods$Ecov_process[m], # "rw" or "ar1"     M_how = array(df.mods$Ecov_how[m],c(1,1,asap3[[1]]$dat$n_ages,1))) # n_Ecov x n_stocks x n_ages x n_regions    mean_map <- NULL   if(df.mods$mean_model[m] == "estimate-M"){     if(df.mods$age_specific[m]) mean_map[1,1,] <- 1:asap3[[1]]$dat$n_ages     else mean_map[1,1,] <- 1   }   M <- list(     mean_model = df.mods$mean_model[m],     re_model = matrix(df.mods$M_re[m], 1,1),     means_map = mean_map   )   if(df.mods$mean_model[m] == "estimate-M" & !df.mods$age_specific[m]) M$initial_means = array(0.28, c(1,1,asap3[[1]]$dat$n_ages)) #n_stocks x n_regions x n_ages    input <- prepare_wham_input(asap3, recruit_model = 2,     model_name = paste0("m",m,": ", df.mods$mean_model[m]," + GSI link: ",df.mods$Ecov_how[m]," + M RE: ", df.mods$M_re[m]),     ecov = ecov,     selectivity=list(model=rep("logistic",6),       initial_pars=c(rep(list(c(3,3)),4), list(c(1.5,0.1), c(1.5,0.1))),       fix_pars=c(rep(list(NULL),4), list(1:2, 1:2))),     NAA_re = list(sigma='rec+1',cor='iid'),     M=M,     age_comp = "logistic-normal-pool0")    # Fit model   mods[[m]] <- fit_wham(input, do.retro=T, do.osa=F) # turn off OSA residuals to save time    # Save model   saveRDS(mod[[m]], file=paste0(df.mods$Model[m],".rds"))    # If desired, plot output in new subfolder   # plot_wham_output(mod=mod, dir.main=file.path(getwd(),df.mods$Model[m]), out.type='html')      # If desired, do projections   # mod_proj <- project_wham(mod)   # saveRDS(mod_proj, file=paste0(df.mods$Model[m],"_proj.rds")) }

code: opt_conv = 1-sapply(mods, function(x) x$opt$convergence) ok_sdrep = sapply(mods, function(x) if(x$na_sdrep==FALSE & !is.na(x$na_sdrep)) 1 else 0) df.mods$conv <- as.logical(opt_conv) df.mods$pdHess <- as.logical(ok_sdrep) df.mods$runtime <- sapply(mods, function(x) x$runtime) df.mods$NLL <- sapply(mods, function(x) round(x$opt$objective,3)) is_conv <- df.mods$conv & df.mods$pdHess which(is_conv) # 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12 mods2 <- mods[is_conv] #mods2[not_conv] <- NULL df.aic.tmp <- as.data.frame(compare_wham_models(mods2, table.opts=list(sort=FALSE, calc.rho=TRUE))$tab) df.aic <- df.aic.tmp[FALSE,] ct = 1 for(i in 1:n.mods){   if(!is_conv[i]){     df.aic[i,] <- rep(NA,5)   } else {     df.aic[i,] <- df.aic.tmp[ct,]     ct <- ct + 1   } } df.aic[,1:2] <- format(round(df.aic[,1:2], 1), nsmall=1) df.aic[,3:5] <- format(round(df.aic[,3:5], 3), nsmall=3) df.aic[grep("NA",df.aic$dAIC),] <- "---" df.mods <- cbind(df.mods, df.aic) rownames(df.mods) <- NULL df.mods

title: Ex 9: Retrospective predictions
text: Setup models m5 (CPI effect recruitment) m3 (CPI effect recruitment) example 2: full state-space model (numbers--age random effects ages, NAA_re = list(sigma='rec+1',cor='iid')) logistic normal age compositions (age_comp = "logistic-normal-pool0") Beverton-Holt recruitment (recruit_model = 3) Cold Pool Index (CPI) fit AR1 process (ecov$process_model = "ar1") CPI “limiting” (e.g. carrying capacity, Iles Beverton (1998)) effect recruitment (ecov$= "recruit", ecov$= 2)
code: env <- list(   label = "CPI",   mean = as.matrix(env.dat$CPI), # CPI observations   logsigma = as.matrix(log(env.dat$CPI_sigma)), # CPI standard error is given/fixed as data   year = env.dat$Year,   use_obs = matrix(1, ncol=1, nrow=dim(env.dat)[1]), # use all obs (=1)   lag = 1, # CPI in year t affects recruitment in year t+1   process_model = "ar1", # fit CPI as AR1 process   where = "recruit", # CPI affects recruitment   how = NA) # fill in by model in loop  # 2 models, with and without CPI effect on recruitment (both fit CPI data to compare AIC) # Model  Recruit_mod  Ecov_mod     Ecov_how #    m1     Bev-Holt       ar1        --- #    m2     Bev-Holt       ar1     Limiting df.mods <- data.frame(Model = c("m1","m2"), Ecov_how = c(0,2), stringsAsFactors=FALSE) n.mods <- dim(df.mods)[1] df.mods

text: model, peel 3-15 years data re-fit model using retro(), project peel 3 years calling project_wham(). projections done F = 0 continuing CPI AR1 process model (without new observations). can specify alternative options projections using $proj.opts (see project_wham() Ex 3: Projections).
code: n.yrs.peel <- 15 n.yrs.proj <- 3 for(m in 1:n.mods){     mods[[m]]$peels <- retro(mods[[m]], ran = unique(names(mods[[m]]$env$par[mods[[m]]$env$random])), n.peels=n.yrs.peel, save.input = T)     for(p in 3:n.yrs.peel) mods[[m]]$peels[[p]] <- project_wham(mods[[m]]$peels[[p]], proj.opts = list(n.yrs = n.yrs.proj, proj.F=rep(0.001,n.yrs.proj))) }

code: plot_retro_pred_R <- function(mods, peels=3:n.yrs.peel, n.yrs.proj=n.yrs.proj){     df <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow=0, ncol=6))     colnames(df) <- c("Year","Model","Peel","Recruitment","termyr")     for(m in 1:length(mods)){         for(p in peels){             tmp <- read_wham_fit(mods[[m]]$peels[[p]])             df <- rbind(df, data.frame(Year=tail(tmp$years_full, n.yrs.proj+1),                                         Model=names(mods)[m],                                         Peel=p,                                         Recruitment=tail(exp(tmp$log_NAA[,1]), n.yrs.proj+1),                                         termyr=c(1,rep(0,n.yrs.proj))))         }         # get full model fit, "peel 0"         tmp <- read_wham_fit(mods[[m]])         df <- rbind(df, data.frame(Year=tmp$years,                                     Model=names(mods)[m],                                     Peel=0,                                     Recruitment=exp(tmp$log_NAA[1:length(tmp$years),1]),                                     termyr=0))     }      df <- subset(df, Year > 1990)     df$Model <- factor(df$Model, levels=names(mods), labels=names(mods))     df$Year <- as.integer(df$Year)      df$Peel <- factor(df$Peel)     dfpts <- subset(df, termyr==1)      cols <- c("black", viridis_pal(option="plasma")(length(levels(df$Peel))-1))     g <- ggplot(df, aes(x=Year, y=Recruitment, linetype=Model, color=Peel, fill=Peel, group=interaction(Model,Peel))) +            geom_line(linewidth=1) +           geom_point(data=dfpts, color='black', size=2, pch=21) +           scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0.01,0.01)) + # breaks=scales::breaks_extended(5)           scale_colour_manual(values=cols) +           scale_fill_manual(values=cols) +           guides(color = "none", fill="none") +           scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0.01,0.01), limits = c(0,NA), labels=wham:::fancy_scientific) +           theme_bw() +           theme(legend.position=c(.9,.9), legend.box.margin = margin(0,0,0,0), legend.margin = margin(0,0,0,0))     return(g) } plot_retro_pred_R(mods, peels=3:n.yrs.peel, n.yrs.proj=n.yrs.proj) ggsave(file.path(write.dir,"retro_pred_R.png"), device='png', width=8, height=5, units='in')

code: make_info <- function(base_years = 1982:2021, ages = 1:10, Fhist = "updown", n_feedback_years = 0) { #changed years     info <- list()     info$ages <- ages     info$years <- as.integer(base_years[1] - 1 + 1:(length(base_years) + n_feedback_years))     na <- length(info$ages)     ny <- length(info$years)     info$n_regions <- 1L     info$n_stocks <- 1L     nby <- length(base_years)     mid <- floor(nby/2)     #up then down      catch_info <- list()     catch_info$n_fleets <- 1L     catch_info$catch_cv <- matrix(0.1, ny, catch_info$n_fleets)     catch_info$catch_Neff <- matrix(200, ny, catch_info$n_fleets)      F_info <- list()     if(Fhist == "updown") F_info$F <- matrix(0.2 + c(seq(0,0.4,length.out = mid),seq(0.4,0,length.out=nby-mid)),nby, catch_info$n_fleets)      #down then up     if(Fhist == "downup") F_info$F <- matrix(0.2 + c(seq(0.4,0,length.out = mid),seq(0,0.4,length.out=nby-mid)),nby, catch_info$n_fleets)      if(n_feedback_years>0) F_info$F <- rbind(F_info$F, F_info$F[rep(nby, n_feedback_years),, drop = F]) #same F as terminal year for feedback period      index_info <- list()     index_info$n_indices <- 1L     index_info$index_cv <- matrix(0.3, ny, index_info$n_indices)     index_info$index_Neff <- matrix(100, ny, index_info$n_indices)     index_info$fracyr_indices <- matrix(0.5, ny, index_info$n_indices)     index_info$units_index <- rep(1, length(index_info$n_indices)) #biomass     index_info$units_index_paa <- rep(2, length(index_info$n_indices)) #abundance     index_info$q <- rep(0.3, index_info$n_indices)          info$maturity <- array(t(matrix(1/(1 + exp(-1*(1:na - na/2))), na, ny)), dim = c(1, ny, na))      L <- 100*(1-exp(-0.3*(1:na - 0)))     W <- exp(-11)*L^3     nwaa <- index_info$n_indices + catch_info$n_fleets + 2     info$waa <- array(NA, dim = c(nwaa, ny, na))     for(i in 1:nwaa) info$waa[i,,] <- t(matrix(W, na, ny))      info$fracyr_SSB <- cbind(rep(0.25,ny))      catch_info$selblock_pointer_fleets <- t(matrix(1:catch_info$n_fleets, catch_info$n_fleets, ny))     index_info$selblock_pointer_indices <- t(matrix(catch_info$n_fleets + 1:index_info$n_indices, index_info$n_indices, ny))     return(list(basic_info = info, catch_info = catch_info, index_info = index_info, F = F_info)) } stock_om_info <- make_info() basic_info <- stock_om_info$basic_info catch_info <- stock_om_info$catch_info index_info <- stock_om_info$index_info F_info <- stock_om_info$F  selectivity_om <- list(   model = c(rep("logistic", catch_info$n_fleets),rep("logistic", index_info$n_indices)),   initial_pars = rep(list(c(5,1)), catch_info$n_fleets + index_info$n_indices) ) #fleet, index  M_om <- list(initial_means = array(0.2, dim = c(1,1, length(basic_info$ages))))  NAA_re_om <- list(   N1_pars = array(exp(10)*exp(-(0:(length(basic_info$ages)-1))*M_om$initial_means[1]), dim = c(1,1,length(basic_info$ages))),   sigma = "rec", #random about mean   cor="iid", #random effects are independent   recruit_model = 2, #random effects with a constant mean   recruit_pars = list(exp(10)),   sigma_vals = array(0.5, c(1,1,length(basic_info$ages))) #sigma_R, only the value in the first age class is used. )  stock_om_input <- prepare_wham_input(   basic_info = basic_info,    selectivity = selectivity_om,    NAA_re = NAA_re_om,    catch_info = catch_info,   index_info = index_info,   M = M_om,     F = F_info )  stock_om <- fit_wham(stock_om_input, do.fit = FALSE, MakeADFun.silent = TRUE) #n_stock x n_regions x n_ages array exp(stock_om_input$par$log_NAA_sigma[1,1,1]) #Rsigma #> [1] 0.5

code: get_F_from_catch <- function(om, year, catch, Finit = 0.1, maxF = 10){     rep = om$rep     naa = rep$NAA[1,1,year,]     Maa = rep$MAA[1,1,year,]     sel_tot = rbind(rep$FAA[,year,]/max(exp(rep$log_FAA_tot[year,]))) #matrix nfleets x n_ages      waa = rbind(om$input$data$waa[om$input$data$waa_pointer_fleets, year,]) #matrix nfleets x n_ages      nfleets <- length(om$input$data$waa_pointer_fleets)     get_catch = function(log_F, naa, sel, waa, Maa){         Faa = exp(log_F) * sel_tot         Zaa = Maa + apply(Faa,2,sum)         Catch = 0         for(a  in 1:length(naa)) for(f in 1:nfleets) Catch = Catch + waa[f,a] * naa[a] * Faa[f,a] *(1 - exp(-Zaa[a]))/Zaa[a];         return(Catch)     }     obj = function(log_F) (catch - get_catch(log_F, naa, sel_tot, waa, Maa))^2     opt = try(nlminb(log(Finit), obj))     if(!is.character(opt)) Fsolve = exp(opt$par)[1] else Fsolve = maxF     if(Fsolve>10) Fsolve = maxF     print(paste0("Fsolve: ", Fsolve))     return(Fsolve) } update_om_F <- function(om, year, catch){     rep <- om$rep #generate the reported values given the parameters     year_ind <- which(om$years == year) #index corresponding to year     Fsolve <- get_F_from_catch(om, year_ind, catch) #find the F for the catch advice      #have to be careful if more than one fleet     FAA <- rbind(rep$FAA[,year_ind,]) #n_fleets x n_ages     age_ind <- om$env$data$which_F_age[year_ind] #which age is used by wham to define total "full F"     old_max_F <- apply(FAA,2,sum)[age_ind] # n_ages     # selAA[[om$env$data$selblock_pointer_fleets[year_ind]]][year_ind,] #this only works when there is a single fleet     selAA <- FAA/old_max_F #sum(selAA[i,]) = 1     new_FAA <- Fsolve * selAA #updated FAA     F_fleet_y <- apply(new_FAA, 1, max) #full F for each fleet     if(om$input$data$F_config==1) {       if(year_ind>1) {         FAA_ym1 <- rbind(rep$FAA[,year_ind-1,]) #n_fleets x n_ages         F_fleet_ym1 <- apply(rbind(FAA_ym1),1,max) #Full F for each fleet in previous year         om$input$par$F_pars[year_ind,] <- log(F_fleet_y) - log(F_fleet_ym1) #change the F_dev to produce the right full F         if(year_ind< NROW(om$input$par$F_pars)){ #change F devs in later years to retain F in those years. Not really necessary for closed loop sims           FAA_yp1 <- rbind(rep$FAA[,year_ind+1,]) #n_fleets x n_ages           F_fleet_yp1 <- apply(rbind(FAA_yp1),1,max) #Full F for each fleet in previous year           om$input$par$F_pars[year_ind+1,] <- log(F_fleet_yp1) - log(F_fleet_y) #change the F_dev to produce the right full F         }       } else om$input$par$F_pars[year_ind,] <- log(F_fleet_y) #if year is the first year of the model, change F in year 1     } else{ #alternative configuration of F_pars       om$input$par$F_pars[year_ind,] <- log(F_fleet)     }     om <- fit_wham(om$input, do.fit = FALSE, MakeADFun.silent = TRUE)     return(om) } update_om_fn = function(om, seed = 123, interval.info = NULL, random = "log_NAA"){   obs_names = c("agg_indices","agg_catch","catch_paa","index_paa", "Ecov_obs", "obsvec")    if(!is.null(interval.info)){ #iteratively update F over assessment interval for the given catch advice     for(y in interval.info$years){       om = update_om_F(om, year = y, catch = interval.info$catch) #put in the right F values       set.seed(seed)       om_sim = om$simulate(complete=TRUE) #resimulate the population and observations       om$input$data[obs_names] = om_sim[obs_names] #update any simulated data       om$input$par[om$input$random] = om_sim[om$input$random] #update any simulated random effects       # reset the om       om <- fit_wham(om$input, do.fit = FALSE, MakeADFun.silent = TRUE)     }   } else { #otherwise just (re)generate the population     set.seed(seed)     om_sim = om$simulate(complete=TRUE) #resimulate the population and observations     om$input$data[obs_names] = om_sim[obs_names] #update any simulated data     om$input$par[random] = om_sim[random] #update any simulated random effects     # reset the om     om <- fit_wham(om$input, do.fit = FALSE, MakeADFun.silent = TRUE)   }   return(om) } make_em_input = function(M_em, sel_em, NAA_em, om_data, em_years){   info = make_info(base_years = em_years) #update the terminal year for the estimation model   ind_em = 1:length(em_years) #year indices   #fill in the data from the operating model simulation   info$catch_info$agg_catch = om_data$agg_catch[ind_em,, drop = FALSE]   info$index_info$agg_indices = om_data$agg_indices[ind_em,, drop = FALSE]   info$catch_info$catch_paa = om_data$catch_paa[,ind_em,, drop = FALSE]   info$index_info$index_paa = om_data$index_paa[,ind_em,, drop = FALSE]   em_input <- prepare_wham_input(     basic_info = info$basic_info,      selectivity = sel_em,      NAA_re = NAA_em,      M = M_em,      catch_info = info$catch_info,     index_info = info$index_info)   return(em_input) } advice_fn = function(em){   #make 5 year projections using F40. Use average SSB/R and YPR inputs over most recent 5 years   proj_opts = list(n.yrs=5, use.FXSPR=TRUE, avg.yrs=tail(em$years,5))    em_proj = project_wham(em, do.sdrep = FALSE, proj.opts = proj_opts, MakeADFun.silent=TRUE) #projected version of the em   advice = mean(apply(em_proj$rep$pred_catch[length(em_proj$years) + 1:5,,drop = FALSE],1,sum)) #mean of the projected catch over the next 5 years fishing at F40   print(advice)   return(advice) } loop_through_fn = function(om, M_em, selectivity_em, NAA_re_em, assess_years, assess_interval = assess.interval, base_years){   catches = numeric() #save the catch advice   for(i in assess_years){     print(i)     #make the input for the estimation model      em_input = make_em_input(M_em, selectivity_em, NAA_re_em, om_data = om$input$data, em_years = base_years[1]:i)     #fit the estimation model     em = fit_wham(em_input, do.sdrep = FALSE, do.retro = FALSE, do.osa=FALSE, MakeADFun.silent = TRUE) #no feedback period yet     #make the catch advice     advice = advice_fn(em)     catches = c(catches, advice)     #set the catch for the next assess_interval years     interval.info = list(catch = advice, years = i + 1:assess_interval)     #update the operating model with the right Fs and resimulate the data given those Fs     om = update_om_fn(om, seed = 123, interval.info = interval.info)     }   return(list(om = om, em  = em, catches = catches)) } stock_om_info <- make_info(base_years = 1982:2021, n_feedback_years = 40) basic_info <- stock_om_info$basic_info catch_info <- stock_om_info$catch_info index_info <- stock_om_info$index_info F_info <- stock_om_info$F  stock_om_input = prepare_wham_input(     basic_info = basic_info,      selectivity = selectivity_om,      NAA_re = NAA_re_om,      M = M_om,    catch_info = catch_info,   index_info = index_info,     F = F_info ) stock_om_input$random <- NULL #so inner optimization won't change simulated RE stock_om <- fit_wham(stock_om_input, do.fit = FALSE, MakeADFun.silent = TRUE) assess.interval = 4 base.years = make_info()$info$years #no feedback period yet first.year = head(base.years,1) terminal.year = tail(base.years,1) assess.years = seq(terminal.year, tail(stock_om$years,1)-assess.interval,by = assess.interval)  stock_om = update_om_fn(stock_om)  looped_res = loop_through_fn(stock_om, M_em = M_em, selectivity_em = selectivity_om, NAA_re_em = NAA_re, assess_years = assess.years, base_years = base.years) looped_rep <- looped_res$om$rep res <- cbind(stock_om$rep$SSB, looped_rep$SSB) plot(stock_om$years, res[,1], type = "l", ylim = c(0,max(res)), ylab = "SSB", xlab = "Year") lines(stock_om$years, res[,2], col = "red") res <- cbind(looped_rep$SSB[1:76]/exp(looped_rep$log_SSB_FXSPR[1:76,1]), looped_res$em$rep$SSB[1:76]/exp(looped_res$em$rep$log_SSB_FXSPR[1:76,1])) plot(stock_om$years[1:76], res[,1], type = "l", ylim = c(0,max(res)), ylab = "SSB/SSB40", xlab = "Year") Could use it in any (single) season move_prior$use_prior[1,1,1,1] <- 1 # sd on logit scale move_prior$prior_sigma <- array(0, dim = c(2,n_seasons,2,1)) move_prior$prior_sigma[1,1,1,1] <- 0.2 move_prior$mean_vals[1,1,1,1] #transform (inverse logit here) of mean of the prior distribution #> [1] 0.3 input_move_prior <- prepare_wham_input(diff_stocks_asap,     basic_info = basic_info,     NAA_re = NAA_list,     selectivity = selectivity,      M = M_in,      F = F_in,      catchability = q_in,     move = move_prior)  c(length(unique(input_move_prior$map$mu_re)), #+1 for NAs length(unique(input_move_prior$map$mu_prior_re))) #+1 for NAs #> [1] 1 2 x <- input_move_prior$par$trans_mu x[] <- as.integer(input_move_prior$map$trans_mu) x[1,,2,1] <- NA input_move_prior$map$trans_mu <- factor(x) #fixed effect estimated in fit_move, use all estimates except the estimated mean movement parameter. ind <- names(fit_move$parList)[!names(fit_move$parList) %in% "trans_mu"] input_move_prior$par[ind] <- fit_move$parList[ind] fit_move_prior <- fit_wham(input_move_prior, do.osa = FALSE, do.retro = FALSE, do.sdrep = FALSE, do.brps = FALSE)  #estimated movement fit_move$rep$mu[1,1,1,1,1,2] #> [1] 0.009262632 fit_move_prior$rep$mu[1,1,1,1,1,2] #> [1] 0.1848194

Stock Miller (2021) describes details model including equations, simulation tests, demos random effects options numbers--age, M, selectivity, environment-recruitment. Stock et al. (2021) describes 2D (year x age) AR(1) correlation structure can used numbers--age, M, selectivity WHAM (Berg Nielsen 2016, Cadigan 2016, Xu et al. 2019). Since , WHAM also extended include covariate random effects index catchability covariate effects M. Miller et al. (2025) provides details latest extension allow multiple regions stocks, possibly covariate random effects movement. Seasonal changes fleet fishing effort movement also possible. version WHAM allows single stock region remains available “single_wham” branch, developed . title: Calculate Akaike's Information Criterion for a WHAM model — aic

title: Compare multiple WHAM (or ASAP) models — compare_wham_models
code: compare_wham_models(   mods,   do.table = TRUE,   do.plot = TRUE,   fdir = getwd(),   compare.opts = NULL,   table.opts = NULL,   plot.opts = NULL )

title: Compare multiple WHAM (or ASAP) models — compare_wham_models
text: mods (named) list fit WHAM/ASAP models. read ASAP model output, use read_asap3_fit. names given, 'm1', 'm2', ... used. .table T/F, produce table AIC /Mohns rho? Default = TRUE. .plot T/F, produce plots? Default = TRUE. fdir character, path directory save table /plots. Default = getwd(). compare.opts list options generate comparison results.  See details various options. table.opts list options AIC/rho table.  See details various options. plot.opts list options plots. See details various options.

title: Compare multiple WHAM (or ASAP) models — compare_wham_models
text: list following components: daic Vector delta-AIC model (.table=T table.opts$calc.aic=T) aic Vector AIC model (.table=T table.opts$calc.aic=T) rho Matrix Mohns rho model (.table=T table.opts$calc.rho=T) best Name best model (lowest AIC) (.table=T table.opts$calc.aic=T) tab Results table AIC Mohns rho (.table=T) g List ggplot2 objects later modification (.plot=T plot.opts$return.ggplot=T)

title: Compare multiple WHAM (or ASAP) models — compare_wham_models
text: optional elements compare.opts list : $stock integer, stock include results. Default = 1. $region integer, region include results. Default = 1. optional elements table.opts list : $fname character, filename save CSV results table (.csv appended). Default = 'model_comparison'. $sort T/F, sort AIC? Default = TRUE. $calc.rho T/F, calculate Mohns rho? Retrospective analysis must run modes. Default = TRUE. $calc.aic T/F, calculate AIC? Default = TRUE. $print T/F, print table console? Default = TRUE. $save.csv T/F, save table CSV file? Default = FALSE. optional elements plot.opts list : $.type character, either 'pdf' 'png' (default = 'png' sure system('pdftk') work across platforms.) $ci vector T/F, length = 1 (applied models) number models $years vector, years plot? Default = (model projection years). $vector, plots make? Default = . See details. $relative.character, name "base" model plot differences relative . $alpha scalar, (1-alpha)% confidence intervals plotted. Default = 0.05 95% CI. $ages.lab vector, overwrite model age labels. $kobe.yr integer vector applied models number models, year use Kobe plot (relative status). Default = terminal model year(s). $M.age integer, age use M time-series plot. Default = max(data$which_F_age) (max age F use full total F). $return.ggplot T/F, return list ggplot2 objects later modification? Default = TRUE. $kobe.prob T/F, print probabilities model quadrant Kobe plot? Default = TRUE. $refpt "XSPR" "MSY", reference point use. Default = "XSPR". $browse Open html document web browser ($.type = 'png') (default = TRUE). plot.opts$specifies plots make: 1 3-panel SSB (spawning stock biomass), F (fully-selected fishing mortality), Recruitment 2 CV (coefficient variation) SSB, F, Recruitment 3 Fleet selectivity (block, averaged across years) 4 Index selectivity (block, averaged across years) 5 Selectivity tile (fleets + indices, useful time-varying random effects) 6 M time series (natural mortality, can specify age plot.opts$M.age) 7 M tile (useful time-varying random effects) 8 3-panel F X% SPR, SSB F_X%SPR, yield F_X%SPR 9 2-panel relative status (SSB / SSB F_X%SPR F / F_X%SPR) 10 Kobe status (relative SSB vs. relative F) plot.opts$return.ggplot = TRUE, list g returned holding ggplot2 objects later modification. g[[]] holds plot corresponding , e.g. g[[2]] CV plot.

code: fit_wham(   input,   n.newton = 3,   do.sdrep = TRUE,   do.retro = TRUE,   n.peels = 7,   do.osa = TRUE,   osa.opts = list(method = "oneStepGaussianOffMode", parallel = TRUE),   do.post.samp = TRUE,   model = NULL,   do.check = FALSE,   MakeADFun.silent = FALSE,   retro.silent = FALSE,   do.proj = FALSE,   proj.opts = list(n.yrs = 3, use.last.F = TRUE, use.avg.F = FALSE, use.FXSPR = FALSE,     proj.F = NULL, proj.catch = NULL, avg.yrs = NULL, cont.ecov = TRUE, use.last.ecov =     FALSE, avg.ecov.yrs = NULL, proj.ecov = NULL, cont.Mre = NULL, avg.rec.yrs = NULL,     percentFXSPR = 100),   do.fit = TRUE,   save.sdrep = TRUE,   do.brps = TRUE,   fit.tmb.control = NULL,   TMB.bias.correct = FALSE,   TMB.jointPrecision = FALSE )

title: Fit WHAM model — fit_wham
text: input Named list components: $data Data fit assessment model . $par Parameters, list parameter objects required user template (random fixed effects). See TMB::MakeADFun. $map Map, mechanism collecting fixing parameters. See TMB::MakeADFun. $random Character vector defining parameters treat random effect. See TMB::MakeADFun. $years Numeric vector years model spans. important model fitting, useful plotting. $model_name Character, name model, e.g. "Yellowtail flounder" $ages.lab Character vector age labels, e.g. c("1","2","3","4+"). n.newton integer, number additional Newton steps optimization. Passed fit_tmb. Default = 3. .sdrep T/F, calculate standard deviations model parameters? See TMB::sdreport. Default = TRUE. .retro T/F, retrospective analysis? Default = TRUE. n.peels integer, number peels use retrospective analysis. Default = 7. .osa T/F, calculate one-step-ahead (OSA) residuals? Default = TRUE. See details. Returned mod$osa$residual. osa.opts list 2 options (method, parallel) calculating OSA residuals, passed TMB::oneStepPredict. Default: osa.opts = list(method="oneStepGaussianOffMode", parallel=TRUE). See make_osa_residuals. .post.samp T/F, obtain sample posterior random effects? Default = TRUE. YET IMPLEMENTED. model (optional), previously fit wham model. .check T/F, check model parameters identifiable? Passed fit_tmb. Runs internal function check_estimability, originally provided https://github.com/kaskr/TMB_contrib_R/TMBhelper. Default = TRUE. MakeADFun.silent T/F, Passed silent argument TMB::MakeADFun. Default = FALSE. retro.silent T/F, Passed argument internal retro function. Determines whether peel number printed screen. Default = FALSE. .proj T/F, projections? Default = FALSE. true, runs project_wham. proj.opts named list following components: $n.yrs (integer), number years project/forecast. Default = 3. $use.last.F (T/F), use terminal year F projections. Default = TRUE. $use.FXSPR (T/F), calculate use F X $use.FMSY (T/F), calculate use FMSY projections. $proj.F (vector), user-specified fishing mortality projections. Length must equal n.yrs. $proj.catch (vector), user-specified aggregate catch projections. Length must equal n.yrs. $avg.yrs (vector), specify years average calculating reference points. Default = last 5 model years, tail(model$years, 5). $cont.ecov (T/F), continue ecov process (e.g. random walk AR1) projections. Default = TRUE. $use.last.ecov (T/F), use terminal year ecov projections. $avg.ecov.yrs (vector), specify years average environmental covariate(s) projections. $proj.ecov (matrix), user-specified environmental covariate(s) projections. n.yrs x n_Ecov. $cont.Mre (T/F), continue M random effects (.e. AR1_y 2D AR1) projections. Default = TRUE. FALSE, M averaged $avg.yrs (defaults last 5 model years). $avg.rec.yrs (vector), specify years calculate CDF recruitment use projections. Default = model years. $percentFXSPR (scalar), percent F_XSPR use calculating catch projections, used proj.opts$use.FXSPR = TRUE. example, GOM cod uses F = 75 $percentFMSY (scalar), percent F_MSY use calculating catch projections, used $use.FMSY = TRUE. .fit T/F, fit model using fit_tmb. Default = TRUE. save.sdrep T/F, save full TMB::sdreport object? FALSE, save summary.sdreport reduce model object file size. Default = TRUE. .brps T/F, calculate report biological reference points. Default = TRUE. fit.tmb.control list optimizer controlling attributes passed fit_tmb. Default list(use.optim = FALSE, opt.control = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)), stats::nlminb used opitmize. TMB.bias.correct T/F whether use bias.correct feature TMB::sdreport. Default = FALSE. TMB.jointPrecision T/F whether TMB::sdreport return joint precision matrix fixed random effects. Default = FALSE.

title: Fit WHAM model — fit_wham
text: fit TMB model additional output specified: $rep List derived quantity estimates (see examples) $sdrep Parameter estimates (standard errors .sdrep=TRUE) $peels Retrospective analysis (.retro=TRUE) $osa One-step-ahead residuals (.osa=TRUE)

title: Fit WHAM model — fit_wham
text: Standard residuals appropriate models random effects. Instead, one-step-ahead (OSA) residuals can used evaluating model goodness--fit (Thygeson et al. (2017), implemented TMB::oneStepPredict). Additional OSA residual options passed TMB::oneStepPredict list osa.opts. example, use (much faster, ~1 sec instead 2 min) full Gaussian approximation instead (default) generic method, can use osa.opts=list(method="fullGaussian").

title: Plot WHAM output — plot_wham_output
text: Generates many output plots tables fit WHAM model.

title: Plot WHAM output — plot_wham_output
code: plot_wham_output(   mod,   dir.main = getwd(),   out.type = "html",   res = 72,   plot.opts = NULL )

title: Plot WHAM output — plot_wham_output
text: mod output fit_wham dir.main character, directory save plots (default = getwd()) .type character, either 'html', 'pdf', 'png' (default = 'html') res resolution save .png files (dpi) plot.opts (optional) list plot modifications

title: Plot WHAM output — plot_wham_output
text: .type = 'html' (default) makes html file viewing plot .png files html tables parameter estimates, numbers age, fishing mortality, spawning stock biomass browser. .type = 'pdf' makes one pdf file plots tables. .type = 'png' creates subdirectory `plots_png“ dir.main saves .png files within. .type = 'pdf' 'png' makes LaTeX pdf files tables parameter estimates. (tabs: 'input data', 'diagnostics', 'results', 'ref_points', 'retro', 'misc'). plot.opts holds optional arguments modify plots: $ages.lab Character vector, change age labels plots (default 1:n.ages). $font.family Font family, e.g. "Times". $browse T/F whether open html file browser. Default = T. $colors Color palette. Options "default", "bw", "gray", "cividis", "warm", "ocean", "forest",       "highcontrast", "pastel", "turbo". Default = "default". Plot functions located wham_plots_tables.R Table function located par_tables_fn.R

code: prepare_projection(model, proj.opts, check.version = FALSE)

title: Prepare input data and parameters to project an already fit WHAM model — prepare_projection
text: model previously fit wham model proj.opts named list following components: $n.yrs (integer), number years project/forecast. Default = 3. $use.last.F (T/F), use terminal year F projections. Default = TRUE. $use.avg.F (T/F), use average F certain years projections. Default = FALSE. Years average determined $avg.yrs defined . $use.FXSPR (T/F), calculate use F X% SPR projections. Default = FALSE. $use.FMSY (T/F), calculate use FMSY projections. Default = FALSE. $proj.F (vector), user-specified fishing mortality projections. Length must equal n.yrs. $proj.catch (vector), user-specified aggregate catch projections. Length must equal n.yrs. $avg.yrs (vector), specify years use average population attributes (MAA,FAA,WAA,maturity,movement) projection years. BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $cont.ecov (T/F), continue ecov process (e.g. random walk AR1) projections. Default = TRUE. $use.last.ecov (T/F), use terminal year ecov projections. $avg.ecov.yrs (vector), specify years average environmental covariate(s) projections. $proj.ecov (matrix), user-specified environmental covariate(s) projections. n.yrs x n.ecov. $cont.M.re (T/F), continue M random effects (.e. AR1_y 2D AR1) projections. Default = FALSE. FALSE, M averaged $avg.yrs.M (defaults last 5 model years). $cont.move.re (T/F), continue movement random effects projections. Default = FALSE. FALSE, movement parameters averaged $avg.yrs.move (defaults last 5 model years). $cont.L.re (T/F), continue L ("extra mortality rate") random effects projections. Default = FALSE. FALSE, L parameters averaged $avg.yrs.L (defaults last 5 model years). $avg.rec.yrs (vector), specify years calculate CDF recruitment use projections. Default = model years. used recruitment estimated fixed effects (SCAA). $percentFXSPR (scalar), percent F_XSPR use projections, used $use.FXSPR = TRUE. example, project F = 75% F_40%SPR, proj.opts$percentFXSPR = 75. Default = 100. $percentFMSY (scalar), percent F_MSY use projections, used $use.FMSY = TRUE stock-recruit relationship assumed. Default = 100. $proj_F_opt (integer vector), integers specifying configure year projection: Overrides specifications. 1: Use terminal F. 2: use average F (years determined $avg.yrs). 3: use F X% SPR. 4: user-specified F ($proj_Fcatch). 5: user-specified catch ($proj_Fcatch). 6: use Fmsy (recruit_model>2). $proj_Fcatch (vector matrix), catch F values use projection year: values used using Fmsy, FXSPR, terminal F average F. Overrides specifications proj.F proj.catch. vector, total catch F supplied else matrix columns fleets fleet-specific F found/used (n.yrs x 1 n_fleets). $proj_mature (array), user-supplied maturity values projection years dimensions (n_stocks x n.yrs x n_ages). $proj_waa (3-d array), user-supplied waa values projection years first third dimensions equal model$input$data$waa (waa source x n.yrs x n_ages). $proj_R_opt (integer) specifying recruitment treated projection years 1: Continue RE processes recruitment. 2: Make projected recruitment consistent average recruitment SPR reference points cancel bias correction NAA projection years. 3: Average recruitment deviations $avg.yrs.R ($sigma = "rec"). 4: recruitment deviations ($sigma = "rec"). $proj_NAA_opt (integer) specifying NAA random effects treated projection years $sigma = "rec+1": 1: Continue RE processes NAA. 2: Average NAA deviations $avg.yrs.NAA. 3: NAA deviations. $proj_NAA_init (scalar), default starting value NAA random effects projection years exp(10), may large enough catch specification. Use change default call project_wham suggests . $proj_F_init F initialize internal newton search annual projected F given user-specifed catch. Default 0.1 $avg.yrs.sel list (length = n_fleets), years average selectivity FAA fleet projection years. BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.waacatch list (length = n_fleets), years average weight age fleet projection years ($proj_waa NULL). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.waassb list (length = n_stocks), years average weight age stock SSB projection years ($proj_waa NULL). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.mature list (length = n_stocks), years average maturity age stock projection years ($proj_mature NULL). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.L list (length = n_regions), years average extra mortality age region projection years ($cond.L.re = FALSE). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.M list (length = n_stocks, list length = n_regions), years average natural mortality age stock region projection years ($cont.M.re = FALSE). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.move list (length = n_stocks, list length = n_regions), years average movement rates age season stock region (beginning interval) projection years ($cont.move.re = FALSE). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.R list (length = n_stocks), years average recruitment deviations stock region projection years ($proj_R_opt = 3). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.NAA list (length = n_stocks, list length = n_regions), years average NAA deviations stock region projection years ($proj_NAA_opt = 2). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, utils::tail(model$years, 5). check.version T/F check whether version WHAM TMB fitted model match version WHAM using projections. Default = TRUE.

title: Prepare input data and parameters for WHAM model — prepare_wham_input
text: recruit_model specifies stock-recruit model. See wham.cpp implementation. = 1 SCAA (without NAA_re option specified) Random walk (NAA_re$sigma specified), .e. predicted recruitment year = recruitment year -1 = 2 (default) Random effects constant mean = 3 Beverton-Holt = 4 Ricker Note: fit_wham allows fitting SCAA model (NAA_re = NULL), estimates recruitment every year separate fixed effect parameters, case stock-recruit function estimated. warning message printed recruit_model > 2 NAA_re = NULL. wish use stock-recruit function expected recruitment, choose recruitment deviations random effects, either age-1 (NAA_re = list(sigma="rec")) ages (NAA_re = list(sigma="rec+1"), "full state-space" model). See details NAA_re specification. ecov specifies environmental covariate data models. See set_ecov full details. selectivity specifies options selectivity, overwrite existing options specified ASAP data file. See set_selectivity full details. M specifies estimation options natural mortality can overwrite M--age values specified ASAP data file. See set_M full details. NAA_re specifies options random effects numbers--age (NAA, .e. state-space model ). See set_NAA full details. NULL, traditional statistical catch--age model fit. catchability specifies options catchability. See set_q full details. NULL asap3 NULL, single catchability parameter index used initial values specified ASAP file. NULL, initial catchabilities indices = 0.3. move specifies options movement multiple regions. See set_move full details. age_comp specifies age composition models fleet(s) indices. See set_age_comp full details. catch_info optional list fishery catch information can used set types observations asap3 file given.  See set_catch full details. Useful setting operating model simulate population processes observations. Also can useful setting structure assessment model asap3 used. index_info optional list survey/index information can used set types observations asap3 file given.  See set_indices full details. Useful setting operating model simulate population processes observations. Also can useful setting structure assessment model asap3 used. basic_info optional list information can used set population types observations asap3 file given. Particularly useful setting operating model simulate population processes observations. Also can useful setting structure assessment model asap3 used. current options : $ages integer vector ages (years) last plus group $years integer vector years population model spans. $n_seasons number seasons within year. $n_fleets number fishing fleets. $fracyr_seasons proportions year season within year (sums 1). $F matrix (length(years) x n_fleets) annual fishing mortality rates fleet initialize model. $waa array ((n_fleets + n_indices + n_stocks) x length(years) x length(ages)) annual weight age fleet, index, spawning biomass stock. $maturity array (n_stocks x length(years) x length(ages)) annual maturity age estimating spawning biomass stock. $fracyr_SSB matrix (n_years x n_stocks) (1 length(years)) yearly proportions (0-1) year calculate spawning biomass. $spawn_seasons vector (n_stocks) seasons stock spawns. $spawn_regions vector (n_stocks) regions stock spawns. $NAA_where array (n_stocks x n_regions x n_ages) 0/1 indicating individuals stock may exist January 1 year. $Fbar_ages integer vector ages use average F age reported "Fbar" across fleets, regions fleet. $q vector (length(n_indices)) catchabilities indices initialize model. $percentSPR (0-100) percentage unfished spawning biomass per recruit determining equilibrium fishing mortality reference point $XSPR_input_average_years years average inputs per recruit calculation (selectivity, M, WAA, maturity) static (prevailing) SPR-based reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)). specific values override option. $average_years_L list (length = n_regions), years average L (extra mortality) per recruit calculation static (prevailing) reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $average_years_M list (length = n_stocks, list length = n_regions), years average M per recruit calculation static (prevailing) reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $average_years_move list (length = n_stocks, list length = n_regions), years average movement parameters per recruit calculation static (prevailing) reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $average_years_mat list (length = n_stocks), years average maturity per recruit calculation static (prevailing) reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $average_years_waassb list (length = n_stocks), years average ssb waa per recruit calculation static (prevailing) reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $average_years_sel list (length = n_fleets), years average selectivity per recruit calculation static (prevailing) reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $average_years_waacatch list (length = n_fleets), years average catch waa per recruit calculation static (prevailing) reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $average_years_SRR list (length = n_stocks), years average SRR parameters static (prevailing) MSY-based reference points. Default last 5 years (utils::tail(1:length(years),5)) $XSPR_R_avg_yrs years average recruitments calculating SPR-based SSB reference points. Default 1:length(years) $XSPR_R_opt 1(3): use annual R estimates(predictions) annual SSB_XSPR, 2(4): use average R estimates(predictions). 5: use bias-corrected expected recruitment. long-term projections, may important use certain years XSPR_R_avg_yrs $FXSPR_init F initialize internal newton search annual static F X percent SPR. Default 0.5 $FMSY_init F initialize internal newton search annual static Fmsy (stock-recruit model assumed). Default 0.5 $simulate_process_error T/F vector (length = 9). simulating model, whether simulate process errors     (NAA, M, selectivity, q, movement, unidentified mortality, q priors, movement priors, Ecov). used applicable random effects. $simulate_observation_error T/F vector (length = 3). simulating model, whether simulate  catch, index, ecov observations. $simulate_period T/F vector (length = 2). simulating model, whether simulate base period (model years) projection period. $bias_correct_process T/F. Perform bias correction log-normal random effects NAA. $bias_correct_BRPs T/F. Perform bias correction analytic SSB/R Y/R bias correction log-normal NAA. May want use XSPR_R_opt = 5 long-term projections. arguments prepare_wham_input provided selectivity, M, age_comp, information provided must consistent basic_info. example dimensions number years, ages, fleets, indices.

title: Project a fit WHAM model — project_wham
text: Provides projections/forecasts existing (already fit) WHAM model.

title: Project a fit WHAM model — project_wham
code: project_wham(   model,   proj.opts = list(n.yrs = 3, use.last.F = TRUE, use.avg.F = FALSE, use.FXSPR = FALSE,     use.FMSY = FALSE, cont.ecov = TRUE, use.last.ecov = FALSE, percentFXSPR = 100,     percentFMSY = 100),   n.newton = 3,   do.sdrep = TRUE,   MakeADFun.silent = FALSE,   save.sdrep = TRUE,   check.version = TRUE,   TMB.bias.correct = FALSE,   TMB.jointPrecision = FALSE )

title: Project a fit WHAM model — project_wham
text: model previously fit wham model proj.opts named list following components: $n.yrs (integer), number years project/forecast. Default = 3. $use.last.F (T/F), use terminal year F projections. Default = TRUE. $use.avg.F (T/F), use average F certain years projections. Default = FALSE. Years average determined $avg.yrs defined . $use.FXSPR (T/F), calculate use F X% SPR projections. Default = FALSE. $use.FMSY (T/F), calculate use FMSY projections. Default = FALSE. $proj.F (vector), user-specified fishing mortality projections. Length must equal n.yrs. $proj.catch (vector), user-specified aggregate catch projections. Length must equal n.yrs. $avg.yrs (vector), specify years use average population attributes (MAA,FAA,WAA,maturity,movement) projection years. BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, tail(model$years, 5). $cont.ecov (T/F), continue ecov process (e.g. random walk AR1) projections. Default = TRUE. $use.last.ecov (T/F), use terminal year ecov projections. $avg.ecov.yrs (vector), specify years average environmental covariate(s) projections. $proj.ecov (matrix), user-specified environmental covariate(s) projections. n.yrs x n.ecov. $cont.M.re (T/F), continue M random effects (.e. AR1_y 2D AR1) projections. Default = FALSE. FALSE, M averaged $avg.yrs.M (defaults last 5 model years). $cont.move.re (T/F), continue movement random effects projections. Default = FALSE. FALSE, movement parameters averaged $avg.yrs.move (defaults last 5 model years). $cont.L.re (T/F), continue L ("extra mortality rate") random effects projections. Default = FALSE. FALSE, L parameters averaged $avg.yrs.L (defaults last 5 model years). $avg.rec.yrs (vector), specify years calculate CDF recruitment use projections. Default = model years. used recruitment estimated fixed effects (SCAA). $percentFXSPR (scalar), percent F_XSPR use projections, used $use.FXSPR = TRUE. example, project F = 75% F_40%SPR, proj.opts$percentFXSPR = 75. Default = 100. $percentFMSY (scalar), percent F_MSY use projections, used $use.FMSY = TRUE stock-recruit relationship assumed. Default = 100. $proj_F_opt (integer vector), integers specifying configure year projection: Overrides specifications. 1: Use terminal F. 2: use average F (years determined $avg.yrs). 3: use F X% SPR. 4: user-specified F ($proj_Fcatch). 5: user-specified catch ($proj_Fcatch). 6: use Fmsy (recruit_model>2). $proj_Fcatch (vector matrix), catch F values use projection year: values used using Fmsy, FXSPR, terminal F average F. Overrides specifications proj.F proj.catch. vector, total catch F supplied else matrix columns fleets fleet-specific F found/used (n.yrs x 1 n_fleets). $proj_mature (array), user-supplied maturity values projection years dimensions (n_stocks x n.yrs x n_ages). $proj_waa (3-d array), user-supplied waa values projection years first third dimensions equal model$input$data$waa (waa source x n.yrs x n_ages). $proj_R_opt (integer) specifying recruitment treated projection years 1: Continue RE processes recruitment. 2: Make projected recruitment consistent average recruitment SPR reference points cancel bias correction NAA projection years. 3: Average recruitment deviations $avg.yrs.R ($sigma = "rec"). 4: recruitment deviations ($sigma = "rec"). $proj_NAA_opt (integer) specifying NAA random effects treated projection years $sigma = "rec+1": 1: Continue RE processes NAA. 2: Average NAA deviations $avg.yrs.NAA. 3: NAA deviations. $proj_NAA_init (scalar), default starting value NAA random effects projection years exp(10), may large enough catch specification. Use change default call project_wham suggests . $proj_F_init F initialize internal newton search annual projected F given user-specifed catch. Default 0.1 $avg.yrs.sel list (length = n_fleets), years average selectivity FAA fleet projection years. BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.waacatch list (length = n_fleets), years average weight age fleet projection years ($proj_waa NULL). BRPs calculated projection years also use . Default = last 5 years, tail(model$years, 5). $avg.yrs.waassb list (length = n_stocks), years average weight age stock SSB projection years ($proj_waa NULL). BRPs calculated projection years also use . BRPs calculated projection years also use . BRPs calculated projection years also use . BRPs calculated projection years also use . BRPs calculated projection years also use . title: Project a fit WHAM model — project_wham
text: WHAM implements five options handling fishing mortality projections. Exactly one must specified proj.opts: Use last year F (default). Set proj.opts$use.last.F = TRUE. WHAM use F terminal model year projections. Use average F. Set proj.opts$use.avg.F = TRUE. WHAM use F averaged proj.opts$avg.yrs projections (done M-, maturity-, weight--age). Use F X% SPR. what: Read an ASAP3 .dat file into R — read_asap3_dat
title: Read an ASAP3 .dat file into R — read_asap3_dat
text: WHAM originally built fit models much like ASAP (Legault Restrepo (1999)) extend include features. function provides functionality use preexisting ASAP3 input data file. output read_asap3_dat passed prepare_wham_input. familiar ASAP3 input files, see ASAP documentation code.

title: Read an ASAP3 .dat file into R — read_asap3_dat
code: read_asap3_dat(filename)

title: Read an ASAP3 .dat file into R — read_asap3_dat
text: filename character vector, names ASAP3 .dat files. file either needs current working directory, filename can include path. multipile files, multi-stock model assumed.

title: Read an ASAP3 .dat file into R — read_asap3_dat
text: named list following components: dat Named list input data parameters comments Comments top ASAP3 .dat file (indicated "#")

title: Read an ASAP3 .dat file into R — read_asap3_dat
Read ASAP3 fit — read_asap3_fit
text: Gets output fit ASAP3 model plotting WHAM models.

title: Read ASAP3 fit — read_asap3_fit
code: read_asap3_fit(wd, asap.name, pSPR = 40)

title: Read ASAP3 fit — read_asap3_fit
text: wd character, directory ASAP3 output files located (ex: 'C://file/directories/model/'). 5 files needed: .rdat, .dat, .std, .cor, .par. asap.name character, base name original .dat file (.e. without .dat extension) pSPR scalar, user-specified percent SPR use reference points, expressed 100*SSBPR(Fspr)/SSBPR(F=0). Default = 40.

title: Read ASAP3 fit — read_asap3_fit
text: named list following elements: $years numeric vector, model years , e.g. 1972:2020 $years_full numeric vector, model + proj years, e.g. 1972:2022. ASAP $years. $selAA list length(n_selblocks), first fleet blocks indices, .e. 4 fleet blocks 3 indices, selAA[[5]] index 1. element matrix, years (rows) x ages (cols), selectivity age $selblock_pointer_fleets matrix, n_years x n_fleets, indices selAA used fleet year $selblock_pointer_indices matrix, n_years x n_indices, indices selAA used index year $MAA matrix, n_years x n_ages, natural mortality $log_SSB matrix, n_years x 2, log-scale spawning stock biomass. 1st col = MLE, 2nd col = SE (.std file ADMB). $log_F matrix, n_years x 2, log-scale fully-selected F. 1st col = MLE, 2nd col = SE (.std file ADMB). $log_NAA matrix, n_years x n_ages, numbers age $NAA_CV matrix, n_years x n_ages, CV numbers age $percentSPR scalar, X% SPR used calculate reference points, default = 40 $log_Y_FXSPR matrix, n_years x 2, log-scale yield FXSPR. 1st col = MLE, 2nd col = SE. $log_FXSPR matrix, n_years x 2, log-scale FXSPR. 1st col = MLE, 2nd col = SE. $log_SSB_FXSPR matrix, n_years x 2, log-scale SSB FXSPR, .e. annual numerator SPR(FXSPR) * Recruits. 1st col = MLE, 2nd col = SE. $log_rel_ssb_F_cov list, length n_years, element 2x2 covariance matrix SSB / SSB_FXSPR first F / F_FXSPR second

what: wham: Woods Hole Assessment Model (WHAM) — wham-package
title: wham: Woods Hole Assessment Model (WHAM) — wham-package
text: Woods Hole Assessment Model (WHAM) general age-structured stock assessment framework can configured estimate assessment models range complexity statistical catch--age (SCAA) model annual recruitments fixed effects, state-space, multi-stock, multi-region, age-structured models many parameters can treated time- age-varying process errors /allowing effects environmental covariates. WHAM generalization code Miller et al. (2016), Miller Hyun (2018), Miller et al. (2018). WHAM also many similarities input data sources ASAP (Legault Restrepo 1999) provides functions generate WHAM input file ASAP3 dat file, although requirement. Many plotting functions input data, results, diagnostics modified code written Chris Legault Liz Brooks.
